events.title: 442nd Regimental Combat Team Movie – Go for Broke!
events.description:
Location: Meeting Room

During World War II, Lt. Michael Grayson is a newly commissioned American Army officer who looks forward to being assigned to the 36th Texas Division. Instead, he is put in charge of Japanese-American soldiers, who form the 442nd Regimental Combat Team. Grayson is bigoted and uneasy about the assignment, but when the unit goes into combat in Italy, he admires their courage and determination. The 442nd eventually becomes the most decorated unit in the U.S. Army.

Because the movie Go for Broke! was released decades before the modern MPAA rating system was established in 1968, it never received a rating. However, if evaluated by modern standards, the film would comfortably fit a PG rating due to its historical war action and complete absence of explicit content. Parental guidance is suggested.

events.title: Hawaii’s Nisei Soldiers of WWII: ​​ Their Significance & Continued Relevance​​  ​
events.description:
Who were the Nisei soldiers of World War II? What did they achieve both during and after the war and why is this still relevant to modern day Hawaiʻi? ​

In honor of Veterans Day, Byrnes Yamashita, president of the Nisei Veterans Legacy, will answer these questions and more in a presentation on the Nisei (second generation Japanese American) soldiers of World War II.​

Yamashita’s overview begins with background on immigration, plantation and post-plantation life, start of the war and incarceration, formation of the all-Nisei Army units, explanation of their exploits during the war, and their post-war contributions.

About the presenter: Yamashita is a retired Navy engineer and the son of a Nisei soldier from Hawaiʻi.

events.title: Book Club – Blood Work and Other Stories by Donald A. Carreira Ching
events.description:
Bamboo Ridge Press’ Donald A. Carreira Ching’s Blood Work and Other Stories won the 2026 Firecracker Award in Fiction.

What we carry. What we inherit. What we leave behind.
Seventeen stories of connection and survival in a place caught between what’s sacred and what’s sold.

On the Windward side of Oʻahu, change moves quick—developers buy up neighborhoods, locals move away, and families struggle to hold on to what remains. Beneath each loss, however, lie quiet acts of resilience that refuse to be forgotten.

Against a backdrop of economic hardship, housing instability, cultural transition, and environmental decline, Donald A. Carreira Ching offers readers a deeply intimate portrait of contemporary Hawai‘i. His characters live in a Hawai‘i far removed from tourist postcards, navigating sorrow, displacement, and the weight of generational trauma. Yet even in these quiet, overlooked corners, they hold fast to the connections that root them in place and community.

With grace and grit, Carreira Ching renders Hawai‘i as few others have, bearing witness to what’s being lost while illuminating what endures: love, memory, and the deep connections between people and place. This collection affirms him as a vital voice in contemporary American fiction and a key contributor to the evolving canon of Hawai‘i literature.

Additional copies of the novel will be available at Kahuku Public and School Library.

events.title: Pokémon Club Tournament
events.description:
Welcome Trainers!

You’ve been practicing – now it’s time to put your knowedge and skills to the test! Have fun, be kind, and do your best! This tournament is about learning, making friends, and enjoying Pokémon together. Welcoming children and teens ages 5-18. Advanced registration is required. Call the library (808-323-7585) to sign up.

Details below:

Tournament Format 

 Everyone plays in every round. 

  • Players will be matched against others with similar records. 
  • No one is eliminated after a loss. 
  • Each round lasts 30 minutes. 
  • Match Points: 
  • Win = 3 points 
  • Tie = 1 point 
  • Loss = 0 points 

After your match is over, report your points to a Judge. The players with the most points at the end of the tournament will be our Tournament Champions!

The Rules

  • Be respectful to all players. 
  • Shake hands, fist bump, or say “Good game” after each match.  
  • Be patient with younger or newer players. 
  • Have fun!
  • Use your own deck or borrow from the library (only one EX/GX/Mega/V card per deck). 
  • Shuffle your deck before each game. 
  • Play to 4 prize cards. 
  • If you need help with a rule, raise your hand for a Judge. Judge decisions are final. 
  • Players will be notified when there are 5 minutes remaining in the match. When time is called the match is over. If no winner is determined, the match is a tie. 

 This program is thanks to a partnership with AASL/ALSC and the Pokémon Company. Additional supplies are generously funded by Friends of the Libraries, Kona (F.O.L.K.).
